title: sdk(ts): add batching_tier typing + examples; test request serialization
author: Monica Patel
description: Context: Runtime/config now supports tiered batching defaults (fast/standard/cost_efficient). This PR updates the TypeScript SDK types and examples so customers can opt into a tier without needing to understand the underlying batching knobs, while keeping the request payload stable and backwards compatible. Also adds a focused serialization test to prevent regressions as we iterate on config surfaces. Changes: 1) Add a typed batching tier field to request options: `batching_tier?: "fast" | "standard" | "cost_efficient"`. 2) Wire `batching_tier` into the request body for chat/completions routes (no behavior change unless provided). 3) Update examples in the repo to show: (a) choosing a tier per route, (b) overriding explicit knobs still works, and (c) recommended guidance for streaming (default: standard unless you have strict token cadence requirements). 4) Add unit tests for request serialization that assert the outbound JSON includes `batching_tier` when set and omits it when undefined; additionally verifies that explicit batching overrides take precedence in the payload when both are provided (SDK-level behavior only; runtime precedence is enforced server-side). Backwards compatibility: No breaking API changes. Existing option shapes remain valid. The new field is optional and does not change defaults. Checklist: - [x] Types updated with docsstrings linking to batching tiers docs - [x] Examples updated (Node + TS) - [x] Serialization tests added for chat/completions - [x] Lint/format passes - [x] Changelog entry added (sdk) Notes: This aligns with the terminology decision to ship `cost_efficient` (not `eco`) in public config. Related: ENG-18426 (SDK examples), PM-413 (tier naming), and SUP-18510 (customer confusion about tier vs explicit overrides).
commits: client: include batching_tier in request options for chat/completions
examples: show tier selection and override precedence
tests: assert request serialization for batching_tier
changed_files: src/client/chat.ts (pass batching_tier into body when provided)
src/client/completions.ts (pass batching_tier into body when provided)
src/internal/serialize.ts (ensure stable JSON output; omit undefined)
review_conversation: Alex Martinez (review): Please make sure we standardize the public string values (cost_efficient vs cost-efficient) and add a small example for ‘set tier per route’. Also, can we guarantee we don’t send `batching_tier: undefined` over the wire? Monica Patel (author): Updated to `cost_efficient` to match config schema + docs PR; added a per-route example in basic-chat and ensured serializer strips undefined keys. Added test coverage. Wei Chen (review): Examples read well, but can we call out streaming sensitivity? We’ve seen customers assume “fast” is always best. Monica Patel (author): Added a note in streaming-chat example recommending `standard` for most streaming use cases and to validate cadence if switching tiers. Ethan Park (review): Minor: confirm precedence expectation in test. We shouldn’t enforce runtime precedence here, just payload behavior. Monica Patel (author): Agreed—test only asserts both fields can be present and are serialized deterministically; comment clarifies server-side precedence. Approvals: Alex Martinez approved; Wei Chen approved; Ethan Park approved.
release_notes: TypeScript SDK: add optional `batching_tier` request option (fast/standard/cost_efficient) and update examples; includes serialization tests to keep payload stable.
